claims.text: returning an array instead of an object prevents future extensibility of the listprunelocks RPC response
claims.quote: This was an Object for future extensibility. No reason to lose that.
claims.status_note: author updated listprunelocks to return an object
claims.status_by_quote: fair enough, I have changed it to return an object.

claims.text: copy prune locks instead of holding cs_main lock while iterating
claims.quote: You could get it as copy and don't keep lock while iterating, performance wise.

claims.text: asks who mentioned the specific users or use cases for the feature
claims.quote: Do you remember at least who mentioned these users/use cases?
claims.status_note: achow101 detailed the wallet rescan use cases
claims.status_by_quote: This is generally useful in the wallet and for any wallets that leverage Bitcoin Core.

claims.text: questioned whether there is real demand or known users to justify adding the RPCs
claims.quote: This looks potentially interesting, but I don't think we should be implementing RPCs when we don't know anyone that would actually be using them?
claims.status_note: achow101 explained wallet rescanning on pruned nodes and stickies-v Concept ACKed
claims.status_by_quote: Thanks for the explanation @achow101 . Concept ACK.

claims.text: include the wallet rescan motivation in the PR description
claims.quote: I think this might be useful to include in PR description to give it more motivation?
claims.status_by_quote: Done, replace that vague part of the description with a better motivation paragraph.

claims.text: iterating over prune locks container without holding lock or copying risks data race
claims.quote: Don't we either have to hold this lock while iterating through the prune locks, or copy them? I think my preference would be to just take a copy here.
claims.status_note: author implemented explicit copy before lock scope ends; reviewer later approved

claims.text: asks why a helper getter is introduced rather than iterating directly
claims.quote: Is there a reason for introducing this helper? Existing validation code that iterates through the locks directly.
claims.status_by_quote: m_prune_locks is private and the direct access to it in validation.cpp is only possible because ChainState is a friend class of BlockManager.

claims.text: asks how prune locks are useful to external applications if they are not persisted across restarts
claims.quote: One thing that is still not clear to me is how this is actually useful to external applications if the locks are not persisted.
claims.status_note: author discussed and added the -prunelockheight startup option which reviewer agreed with and approved

claims.text: asks if the startup option can cause -prune to not be respected
claims.quote: Can't there be a case wherein this new argument causes the -prune=<n> option to not be respected?
claims.status_note: author confirmed that is the intended behavior of prune locks and pointed to PR 21726
claims.status_by_quote: Yes, unless I am misunderstanding your question that is the whole idea behind prune locks

claims.text: asks if INITIAL_BLOCKS in functional test can be halved
claims.quote: Is this correct? The following diff passes where this value is halved along with the corresponding heights in the pruneblockchain RPCs.
claims.status_note: author noted the diff fails locally and kept the minimum reliable value
claims.status_by_quote: for me the proposed diff fails because the blocks are not enough to get actual pruning.

claims.text: suggested improving test assertion since prune_height_locked is -1
claims.quote: prune_height_locked is -1 because the lock prevents the pruning from happening. I don't see much point in asserting that prune_height_unlocked is greater than prune_height_locked.
claims.status_note: author changed test to check explicitly for -1 and >0
claims.status_by_quote: Changed this to check for -1 and >0 more explicitly now.

claims.text: add release notes for the new RPCs and startup option
claims.quote: The changes in this file require a release note because of new RPCs being added. Along with the new startup option.
claims.status_by_quote: Right, added the necessary release notes!

claims.text: asks whether allowing prune locks on future block heights is intentional
claims.quote: There isn't a check that forbids locking blocks that'd be generated in the future. Is it intentional?
claims.status_note: author explained it can be useful and added a documentation note
claims.status_by_quote: Right, that's a good observation, I didn't think about this explicitly so far but I don't see harm in allowing this and it may even be useful for some use-cases.

claims.text: explicitly mention in init.cpp help that -prunelockheight causes -prune to not be respected
claims.quote: Ok, can add a sentence here that this option will cause the -prune option to not be respected - just to be explicit.
claims.status_note: author added the note to help text

claims.text: add functional test for wallet exercising prune locks
claims.quote: Also, a functional test for wallet exercising prune locks that solves the above scenario would be nice.
claims.status_note: author added a functional test covering wallet prune locks
claims.status_by_quote: I added this in a separate commit. I folded it into the existing test file since generating all those blocks is pretty expensive

claims.text: mention in release notes that the init lock can be viewed and removed by RPC
claims.quote: Maybe mention here that the lock may be viewed by `listprunelock`and removed by `setprunelock`.
claims.status_note: author updated release notes and adjusted prefix to user: to allow removing it via RPC
claims.status_by_quote: I changed this and renamed the prefix to `user:` since it's not strictly used by RPCs anymore.

claims.text: questioned whether manual prune locks are needed over using -prune=1 and pruneblockchain RPC
claims.quote: I'm not sure I find the motivation compelling. Would the same functionality be achieved via the `pruneblockchain` RPC and a `-prune=1` setting?
claims.status_note: author explained that managing manual pruning from an external wallet requires reimplementing automatic pruning logic
claims.status_by_quote: Partly yes, but I think it would be much more complex and difficult to implement managing that behavior on the side of an external wallet.

support.reason: This is generally useful in the wallet and for any wallets that leverage Bitcoin Core. The fundamental issue is that if the wallet is not loaded while the node is running, blocks necessary for rescanning when the wallet is loaded may be pruned away.
Enabling wallets to build on top of a pruned node via RPC seems enough of a use case to move this forward.
